Use this page to find maintained references for a study and keep its SCGSim package and PDK revisions paired. The current SCGSim baseline is `2.0.0rc15` at [`fb8cbe1`](https://github.com/NCUPHY-LTLab/scgsim/tree/fb8cbe199386bbe6d81cc9c58817fbe7d339573f).

The public Xmon and CPW examples use OrPen SC PDK revision [`35b4dc1`](https://github.com/NCUPHY-LTLab/orcapen-sc-pdk/tree/35b4dc1cdd3f921badcac2fe57a98366315ae8d9), distributed as `orpen-sc-pdk` and imported as `orpen_sc_pdk`. Use the pinned revision named by the example you follow.

## Keep source revisions paired

For Xmon and CPW, pair SCGSim `2.0.0rc15` with the pinned PDK revision above. The distribution name is `orpen-sc-pdk`; Python imports use `orpen_sc_pdk`. Keep each study's source revision in its environment and record.

The [historical Circular Pad setup](history/curved-source-installation.qmd) records a separate set of pinned SCGSim, PDK and native Palace revisions for that study. Use those pins when reproducing that specific run; the `orpen_sc_pdk` import name also appears in the Xmon and CPW source revision above.

## Native and offline EPR steps

`analyze_epr` evaluates retained saved fields through native AEDT and requires an explicitly selected AEDT release and license. `reanalyze_epr` updates assumptions on a resolved EPR result offline. Follow the complete [saved-field lesson](course/aedt-saved-fields.qmd), then use the [generated API reference](api/analyze_epr.qmd) for its callable signature.

## Junction capacitance reference

For one junction in a given mode and pass, $V$ is its complex peak-phasor voltage and $U_{norm}$ is the electric-energy normalization, not total electric-plus-magnetic energy. For nonzero $V$, the effective modal capacitance is $C_{mode}=2U_{norm}/|V|^2$, the branch capacitance is $C_j=2U_{C,j}/|V|^2$, and the participation ratio is $p_{C,j}=C_j/C_{mode}$. At $V=0$, the ratio is undefined. The [AEDT runtime contract](specs/aedt-runtime.qmd#surface-estimates-and-junction-normalization) records the full voltage, energy and normalization definitions.
